outcome: The general conjecture (every forest T is χ-bounding) remains fully open, but new tree/graph families have been confirmed to satisfy it since 26 January 2024, most notably all 'multibrooms' (Nguyen, Scott & Seymour, 'Trees and near-linear stable sets', arXiv:2409.09397, first posted 2024-09-14), plus narrower results on radius-three tree families and on boxicity-bounded graphs for a 'polynomial' strengthening of the conjecture.
summary: The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (every forest T is χ-bounding: graphs with no induced copy of T and bounded clique number have bounded chromatic number) remains open as a whole. Since 26 January 2024 the strongest genuine advance on the exact stated question is Nguyen, Scott & Seymour, 'Trees and near-linear stable sets' (arXiv:2409.09397, posted 2024-09-14, revised 2025-07-18): they prove that for every forest H, graphs excluding induced H with bounded clique number have a stable set of size |G|^(1-o(1)) (a near-linear but not fully linear bound, so this alone does not establish χ-boundedness), and separately prove the full linear-stable-set / χ-bounding statement for the class of 'multibrooms', a genuinely new family of trees for which the conjecture is now confirmed — this is scope-correct progress and I classify it as `partial` with direction `confirmed`. The triage-flagged 'A Note on the Gyárfás–Sumner Conjecture' (arXiv:2302.08922, same authors, posted 2023-02-17, journal version Graphs and Combinatorics 2024) predates the window (posted before 26 January 2024, journal publication is a later date for the same work and per §6.3 the event date is the first written argument, not the journal date) and in any case proves only a weaker 'path-induced' relaxation of the conjecture, not an induced copy — a related, strictly weaker statement, so it would not count as a case even if it were in-window. Also examined: 'Polynomial Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture for graphs of bounded boxicity' (arXiv:2407.16882, 2024-07-23) — this proves a *polynomial* χ-bound (a strictly stronger conjecture than the stated one) restricted to boxicity-bounded graphs, i.e. both a narrower hypothesis and a stronger conclusion than the stated bullet, making it a related/variant result rather than a case of the stated conjecture, so it does not move this record's status; 'On polynomially high-chromatic pure pairs' (arXiv:2504.21127, revised through 2026-01) extends the same polynomial-conjecture line (brooms/forest unions) and is likewise about the stronger polynomial variant. The oriented-tree, signed-graph, domatic, and rainbow-path papers found by triage are all variants over different objects (digraphs, signed graphs, domatic number) and correctly excluded per §3.1. No result anywhere in the search involved an AI system in producing mathematics: no paper's methods, acknowledgements or announcements credit a model with any part of a proof, bound, or construction. A GitHub repository ('vibemathing/problem-wikipedia-...') targeting this exact conjecture was found and inspected; it is an empty scaffold/template for a prospective AI-assisted research workflow with no mathematical content, results, or claims — not an instance of AI involvement in this problem, and not counted.
competing_reading: One could argue the near-linear stable-set bound in 'Trees and near-linear stable sets' for general forests is itself 'progress' on the whole conjecture (since a large stable set is a weaker consequence one might hope χ-boundedness implies), which would support classifying the overall record as `progress` rather than `partial`. I chose `partial` because the multibroom result is a genuine, clean settlement of the actual χ-boundedness statement for a specific tree family — a case, not merely a bound — which is the stronger and more defensible classification under §6.1's ordering (a settled case outranks a mere quantitative shift). The general near-linear-stable-set result for all forests remains `progress`-flavored on its own but is subsumed by reporting the multibroom case as the decisive event.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture for all forests, or explicit tracking of whether the boxicity/polynomial-conjecture line of work is ever judged by experts to bear on the original (non-polynomial) conjecture's truth.

judgement.doubts: Polynomial-bound results for brooms (2504.21127) would imply χ-boundedness for those trees and could arguably be cases rather than variants; either way the tier stays partial. The near-linear stable-set result for all forests is a bound-type statement subsumed by the multibroom case.
